activity.notes: Lieutenant General Tadamichi Kuribayashi (1891–1945) was appointed to command Japanese defenses on Iwo Jima in 1944 and organized underground and mutually supporting defensive positions before the U.S. assault of February–March 1945. This bounded 1944–1945 activity includes defensive preparations and the Iwo Jima battle, not an assertion that he ruled the island as a sovereign politician, that he won the battle, or that his actions alone determined subsequent strategic decisions. Sources disagree on details of his precise death, so no day-specific death or term-end is invented. The activity is attached to the historical Empire of Japan as military command.

sources.title: Battle of Iwo Jima — U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command
sources.citation_text: The U.S. Navy official history identifies Kuribayashi as commander of Japanese forces, assigned in June 1944, and documents his defensive preparations and 1945 battle.

sources.title: H-042-1: Iwo Jima, Nightmare in Hell — U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command
sources.citation_text: U.S. Navy command history documents Kuribayashi's Japanese army forces on Iwo Jima, February–March 1945, and their defensive positions.

sources.title: Closing In: Marines in the Seizure of Iwo Jima — U.S. Marine Corps
sources.citation_text: U.S. Marine Corps official monograph identifies Lieutenant General Kuribayashi as commander of the 109th Division and Ogasawara Army Group on Iwo Jima.
